section: Wind energy - potential, installed capacity, offshore wind policy, hybrid wind-solar policy
subsections: Wind-Solar Hybrid Policy 2018 and round-the-clock power

accepted.s: The nodal agency for offshore wind energy development in India is:
accepted.x: The National Institute of Wind Energy (NIWE) is the nodal agency for offshore wind energy development.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the nodal agency from related renewable-energy institutions.

accepted.s: The National Offshore Wind Energy Policy, 2015 primarily provides a framework for developing offshore wind farms in India's:
accepted.x: The policy provides the framework for offshore wind farms in India's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ).
accepted.tq: Test the exact geographical scope of a policy.

accepted.s: The initial offshore wind development zones identified for India are located off the coasts of:
accepted.x: The identified zones are off the Gujarat coast and the Tamil Nadu coast, including the Gulf of Mannar.
accepted.tq: Use location-based elimination among coastal states.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the offshore wind Viability Gap Funding scheme:
1. It was approved in 2024.
2. It covers the first 1 GW of offshore wind projects.
3. It provides 500 MW each off Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The scheme approved in 2024 covers 1 GW, divided equally between Gujarat and Tamil Nadu, with an outlay of ₹7,453 crore.
accepted.tq: Combine the approval year, capacity and geographical split.

accepted.s: The Viability Gap Funding approved for the first 1 GW of offshore wind projects amounts to:
accepted.x: The approved VGF scheme provides ₹7,453 crore for the first 1 GW of offshore wind projects.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the project-specific funding figure from other energy-sector outlays.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Partner)
a. United Kingdom
b. Denmark
c. Belgium

a. Offshore Wind Taskforce, February 2026
b. Agreement of 2019, renewed in May 2025
c. Reaffirmation at WEF 2026

List-II (Cooperation)
i. India-Belgium
 ii. India-Denmark
 iii. India-UK
accepted.x: The United Kingdom is associated with the Offshore Wind Taskforce, Denmark with the 2019 agreement renewed in May 2025, and Belgium with the WEF 2026 reaffirmation.
accepted.tq: Start from the distinctive date and institutional pair.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT an advantage generally associated with offshore wind energy?
o: Lower maintenance and installation costs than onshore wind
accepted.x: Offshore wind generally benefits from stronger, steadier winds and less land conflict, but it is costlier and harder to maintain than onshore wind.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed comparison in the list of advantages and disadvantages.

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes the National Wind-Solar Hybrid Policy, 2018?
o: It replaces wind power with solar power in all renewable-energy parks.
It permits only separate wind and solar plants connected to different grids.
It restricts hybrid projects to off-grid rural applications.
It promotes wind turbines and solar photovoltaic systems at the same grid connection point.
accepted.x: The policy promotes co-location of wind turbines and solar PV at the same point of grid connection.
accepted.tq: Test the precise operational definition of a policy.
accepted.sec: Wind-Solar Hybrid Policy 2018 and round-the-clock power

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about wind-solar hybrid projects:
1. They can improve the use of land and transmission infrastructure.
2. They can reduce variability in renewable power generation.
3. They are intended only for isolated micro-grids.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Hybrid projects are also designed for large grid-connected systems, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Reject the restrictive word 'only' and retain the two stated benefits.
accepted.sec: Wind-Solar Hybrid Policy 2018 and round-the-clock power

accepted.s: Round-the-clock renewable-energy tenders generally combine:
accepted.x: RTC renewable-energy tenders bundle wind, solar and storage to provide a firm supply of electricity.
accepted.tq: Identify the components of a bundled power-supply model.
accepted.sec: Wind-Solar Hybrid Policy 2018 and round-the-clock power

accepted.s: The waiver of ISTS charges for eligible renewable-energy projects applied to projects commissioned by:
accepted.x: The ISTS-charge waiver applied to eligible projects commissioned by 30 June 2025.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a specific deadline from nearby policy dates.
accepted.sec: Wind-Solar Hybrid Policy 2018 and round-the-clock power

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the financing pattern of Intra-State Green Energy Corridor-I?
accepted.x: The financing pattern is MNRE 40%, KfW 40% and the States 20%.
accepted.tq: Match each contributor with its precise percentage share.
accepted.sec: Wind-Solar Hybrid Policy 2018 and round-the-clock power

accepted.s: Repowering of a wind turbine means:
o: Moving an old turbine to a different State without changing its equipment
Converting a wind farm entirely into a solar park
Reducing the height and capacity of existing turbines
Replacing ageing turbines with larger and modern turbines at the same site
accepted.x: Repowering replaces ageing, less efficient turbines with more powerful modern units at the same windy site to increase generation.
accepted.tq: Apply the definition to a practical wind-farm situation.

accepted.s: The first National Repowering Policy for wind turbines was issued in:
accepted.x: The National Repowering Policy was issued in 2016.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the original policy year and the later revision.

accepted.s: The National Repowering Policy, 2016 was revised as the:
accepted.x: The 2016 policy was revised as the Repowering and Life Extension Policy, 2023.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact title of the revised policy from similar-sounding alternatives.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT listed as a support measure relevant to wind-energy development and repowering?
o: Generation Based Incentive for projects before 31 March 2017
Universal waiver of all transmission charges for projects commissioned after 2030
accepted.x: Accelerated depreciation, the pre-31 March 2017 GBI, the Wind RPO trajectory up to 2030 and tariff-based bidding are listed support measures. A universal waiver after 2030 is not stated as a support measure.
accepted.tq: Identify the invented policy condition among genuine incentives.

accepted.s: The Generation Based Incentive mentioned for wind projects applied to projects established before:
accepted.x: The Generation Based Incentive referred to projects established before 31 March 2017.
accepted.tq: Focus on the qualifying cut-off date rather than the general incentive name.

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh is recognised as one of how many windy States in India?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh is one of the eight windy States identified for wind-energy development.
accepted.tq: Test the exact count in a State classification.

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh accounts for what share of India's renewable-energy potential?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh holds 9.10% of India's renewable-energy potential.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the precise percentage from nearby plausible shares.

accepted.s: The principal wind-farm cluster in Andhra Pradesh is located in:
o: North Coastal Andhra around Srikakulam and Vizianagaram
Coastal Andhra around Kakinada and Machilipatnam
Rayalaseema, particularly Ananthapuramu, Kurnool and YSR Kadapa
accepted.x: Wind farms are concentrated in Rayalaseema, especially in Ananthapuramu, Kurnool and YSR Kadapa districts.
accepted.tq: Use regional clustering to identify the correct geographical zone.

accepted.s: Ramagiri in Andhra Pradesh is notable for hosting a:
accepted.x: Ramagiri hosts a hybrid solar-wind park.
accepted.tq: Link a specific place with its distinctive energy project.

accepted.s: According to the stated 2025–26 figure, Andhra Pradesh's installed wind capacity is:
accepted.x: The stated 2025–26 installed wind capacity of Andhra Pradesh is 4,397.67 MW, making wind its second-largest renewable-energy source after solar.
accepted.tq: Separate the current figure from the earlier capacity and future projection.

accepted.s: Which company is identified as the largest wind developer in Andhra Pradesh, with more than 1,700 MW?
accepted.x: Suzlon is identified as Andhra Pradesh's largest wind developer, with more than 1,700 MW.
accepted.tq: Match the company with its State-level development role.

accepted.s: Suzlon's S144 blade unit in Andhra Pradesh is located at:
accepted.x: The S144 blade unit is located at Hulikera in Kanekal mandal of Anantapur.
accepted.tq: Test a precise industrial-location association.

accepted.s: The S144 blade unit at Hulikera was opened on:
accepted.x: The S144 blade unit at Hulikera was opened on 25 August 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the inauguration date from another 2026 energy-sector date.

accepted.s: The Central Electricity Authority projects Andhra Pradesh's wind capacity at approximately:
accepted.x: The CEA projects Andhra Pradesh's wind capacity at 8,257 MW and has indicated the need for an additional 4,200 MW to meet the RPO requirement up to 2035–36.
accepted.tq: Separate a future capacity projection from current installed capacity.

accepted.s: The CEA has indicated that Andhra Pradesh requires an additional wind capacity of about how much to meet its RPO up to 2035–36?
accepted.x: The CEA has indicated that Andhra Pradesh needs about 4,200 MW more to meet its RPO requirement up to 2035–36.
accepted.tq: Identify the incremental requirement rather than the total projected capacity.

accepted.s: Which climatic phenomenon was expected to reduce wind and hydropower output?
o: A positive Indian Ocean Dipole accompanied by heavy rainfall
Western disturbances accompanied by a cold wave
El Niño accompanied by a weak monsoon
La Niña accompanied by a strong monsoon
accepted.x: El Niño and a weak monsoon were expected to dent wind and hydro output.
accepted.tq: Connect the climatic condition with its stated energy-sector impact.

accepted.s: The quantity of solar-wind electricity reported as curtailed in the preceding year was:
accepted.x: The reported curtailment of solar-wind electricity was 2.1 TWh.
accepted.tq: Handle the decimal and unit carefully in a quantitative current-affairs fact.

accepted.s: A grid-variability incident involving oscillations from renewable energy generation in Rajasthan was reportedly felt at:
accepted.x: An oscillation originating from renewable-energy variability in Rajasthan was reportedly felt at Kudankulam.
accepted.tq: Match the reported grid event with its affected power station.

accepted.s: According to the comparative cost assessment stated for 2025, which source was the cheapest new electricity source globally?
accepted.x: Onshore wind was identified as the cheapest source of new electricity globally, with costs falling by 4% in 2025.
accepted.tq: Avoid reversing the onshore–offshore cost comparison.

accepted.s: The cost of onshore wind electricity fell by what percentage in 2025?
accepted.x: The stated fall in the cost of onshore wind electricity in 2025 was 4%.
accepted.tq: Select the precise percentage rather than a rounded alternative.

accepted.s: India's turbine manufacturing capacity is approximately how much per year, with indigenisation of about 70–80%?
accepted.x: India's turbine manufacturing capacity is about 24 GW per year, with 70–80% indigenisation.
accepted.tq: Combine the annual manufacturing capacity with its indigenisation context.

accepted.s: Which of the following demands has been raised by the wind industry?
o: Removal of all renewable purchase obligations
Exclusive government ownership of wind farms
PLI for large forgings and export incentives
A ban on domestic turbine manufacturing
accepted.x: The industry has sought a Production Linked Incentive for large forgings and export incentives.
accepted.tq: Identify the genuine industry-policy demand among reversed alternatives.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about wind-energy policy support:
1. Accelerated depreciation is a support measure.
2. Wind RPO has a trajectory up to 2030.
3. Tariff-based bidding is used as a support mechanism.
4. ISTS-charge waiver was linked to projects commissioned by 30 June 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct and represent the listed forms of support or policy facilitation for renewable-energy projects.
accepted.tq: Check each policy instrument independently before selecting the complete combination.
